_comment.purpose: High-confidence end-to-end delay measurement for the current 112x112, 400 us exposure, 1457 Hz, 100 Hz / 80% pulsed-beam steering setup. It measures command -> DAC -> FSM -> exposure/readout -> current moment-output fit_com separately on x and y.
_comment.method: Each axis uses 128 repetitions of a 1023-chip PRBS and rejects flagged dark/partial-light frames. The suite repeats the complete measurement at 0.06, 0.10 and 0.15 V. A usable answer must pass correlation SNR, phase residual, live coverage, per-burst MAD, phase-versus-correlation agreement, and <=0.15-frame amplitude invariance gates.
_comment.why_it_handles_jitter: The coded drive is uncorrelated with ambient beam motion, so averaging 128 identical bursts suppresses ordinary jitter by sqrt(N). Each burst is also estimated independently: nonstationary jitter appears as MAD and fails the run. The 283-frame quiet interval walks the burst against the 100 Hz light phase, rejected frames are removed rather than held, and 100 Hz harmonics are excluded from the phase fit.
_comment.result: fsm_delay_robust_100hz_80pct.pdf plus six individual PDF/.dat/_traces.dat records. Copy no delay unless all six quality verdicts pass and each axis's three estimates span <=0.15 frame.
